My Journey & Philosophy

From the countryside of Homabay to medical training, literature, and social reform.

I am Wanga Domnic Okoth, a second born in a family of three raised in Rangwe Constituency, West Gem Ward, Homabay County, in the Kenyan countryside away from the shores of Lake Victoria. Growing in the countryside never limited the horizons I imagined for myself or the opportunities I believed life could offer. Graced to be raised by parents who believed in me, encouraged curiosity and open mindedness, promoted ingenuity and shaped my worldview in ways that continue to influence how I interact with people, society and the world.

My learning began long before I started schooling but first stepped into a classroom at Heartspring Junior Academy where I undertook my primary education, before proceeding to Kabianga School for my secondary education. I am currently pursuing my medical studies at Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT) where through meeting humanity at its rawest form I have come to realise and of the strong opinion that healthcare must extend beyond diagnosis and treatment of disease to recognising the dignity, experiences and humanity of the individual whose worldview has been shaken by the ailment.

As an essential part of medicine I'm strongly committed to mental health, an area in which I am actively involved through the Healed Healers Community Based Organisation. I am particularly interested in the intersection of human wellbeing, psychological health and the broader social conditions that shape our lives.

Literature occupies a very important place in my life. I have always been drawn to stories and their abilities to articulate experiences that would otherwise remain unspoken. I believe that through literature human beings find their purest voices and through relatable stories we learn to identify and interact with each not as strangers but as those connected to us through similar experiences. Through literature I explore the human conditioning, question society and look for meaning in questions that do not always have easy answers in a complex world.

Published Works

Books exploring ambition, morality, faith, mortality, and the human condition.

Book One

Dare Dream

Dare Dream is a powerful story of ambition, hope, identity, the courage to imagine a different future, and what it truly means to realise change. It challenges readers to push past assigned limitations and envision transformative possibilities.

Book Two

Beyond the White Coat

What happens when the pursuit of a childhood dream brings you face to face with questions that you have never taken interest in and worse still to which humanity has not given any credible answers? Beyond the White Coat follows Brian, a young medical student who encounters culture shock, formaldehyde-filled laboratories, unforgiving instructors, and existential encounters with life, death, faith, and love.

Convictions & Advocacy

Pan-Africanist philosophy, institutional reform, and confronting uncomfortable truths.

Pan-Africanist Vision

A Pan Africanist at heart I believe deeply in the restoration of Africans dignity as humans who can contribute to global intellectual conversations and not as subhumans to be conquered. The historical and continued alienation of African people and global systems that have sustained inequality continue to be issues of great importance when it comes to my understanding of the world.

I hold the conviction that Africa's transformation is possible through selfless and servanthood leadership, as it was in our culture before colonisation, accountable institutions, sound policies and systems and a people willing to question the realities that shape its societies.

Fearless Truth & Education

I'm of the view that a society can never change unless the reality is confronted and I believe the time is right that we learn to tell ourselves hard uncomfortable truths and ask the difficult questions especially the ones that we have learnt to avoid over the years.

Ultimately I am of great interest in questions that connect medicine, mental health, literature, African history and current affairs, society and humanity. Education to me is not merely a means of personal development but an opportunity to acquire knowledge, perspective and capacity to meaningfully engage with and contribute to the world around me.
